claim.qualifier: EPA combined-cycle range for 2025 ID.4 AWD Pro S

reality.qualifier: Car and Driver instrumented 75 mph highway range test on a 2024 ID.4 Pro S AWD measured 240 mi — same as the 2021 model they previously tested. Recharged owner data: 190–215 mi typical at 70–75 mph for the AWD Pro S.
reality.verbatim_quote: In our 75-mph highway range test, the Pro S AWD managed 240 miles, matching the distance of the 2021 model we've previously tested.

sources.name: Car and Driver — 2024 Volkswagen ID.4 Tested
Recharged — VW ID.4 Real-World Highway Range

narrative_one_liner: VW ID.4 AWD Pro S advertised 263 mi EPA; Car and Driver 75 mph test 240 mi (~9% gap).
narrative: VW advertises 263 mi EPA combined for the ID.4 AWD Pro S. Car and Driver's instrumented 75 mph highway test measured 240 mi — a 9% gap. Recharged owner data shows typical 70–75 mph range of 190–215 mi for the AWD trim, suggesting most owners see somewhat larger real-world gaps than the C/D test methodology captures. The relatively modest 9% gap places ID.4 in the middle of the dataset's distribution.
methodology_notes: Car and Driver tests at 75 mph (not 70), making the result more conservative than CR's 70 mph methodology would. Even so, the 9% gap is moderate.
caveats: 75 mph C/D test is harsher than CR 70 mph methodology; result would likely improve at 70 mph.
Earlier ID.4 RWD trims have shown closer-to-EPA performance (sometimes beating EPA in mixed driving). The AWD Pro S is the worst-case for ID.4 family efficiency.
alternative_explanations: AWD adds weight and motor friction; the 9% gap is consistent with general AWD-EV penalty.
Pro S trim adds heavier interior content (panoramic glass, larger wheels) vs base Pro.
